title: ASEAN, APEC and SAARC

cards.b:
Asia has built regional groups very different from the EU. ASEAN is the most successful, a loose but durable community of 11 South-East Asian states. APEC is a trans-Pacific forum of 21 economies that works by voluntary goals. SAARC, India's own neighbourhood grouping, has been frozen for a decade.

UPSC asks why ASEAN succeeded where SAARC failed, what the "ASEAN Way" means, why India is outside APEC, and how BIMSTEC is replacing SAARC in India's policy. These link directly to Paper II Section B: Act East, the Indo-Pacific and South Asia.

Know the founding dates, members, key agreements and the latest state of each, and be ready to compare.

The Bangkok Declaration of 8 August 1967 founded ASEAN with Indonesia, Malaysia, the Philippines, Singapore and Thailand. It was partly a Cold War bloc against communist spread, and a way to calm quarrels among members (such as Indonesia's "Konfrontasi" with Malaysia).

Timor-Leste became the 11th member on 26 October 2025 at the Kuala Lumpur summit. The Philippines chairs ASEAN in 2026.

The ASEAN Way

Consensus (musyawarah and mufakat), non-interference in internal affairs, quiet diplomacy, informality and respect for sovereignty. Codified in the Treaty of Amity and Cooperation (1976), which outside powers including India (2003), China and the US have also signed.
  • ASEAN Charter (2007, in force 2008) gave legal personality. Secretariat in Jakarta.
  • ASEAN Community (2015) with three pillars: political-security, economic and socio-cultural.
  • AFTA (1992) and the ASEAN Economic Community.
  • ASEAN centrality: ASEAN hosts wider forums: ASEAN Regional Forum (1994), ASEAN Plus Three (1997), East Asia Summit (2005), ADMM-Plus (2010).
  • RCEP (signed November 2020, in force January 2022): ASEAN plus China, Japan, South Korea, Australia and New Zealand. India left the talks in November 2019.

Amitav Acharya, Constructing a Security Community in Southeast Asia (2001), applies constructivism to ASEAN.

• Myanmar. After the February 2021 coup, ASEAN's Five-Point Consensus (April 2021) went largely unimplemented. Myanmar's junta leaders were barred from summits.
  • South China Sea. Members split: the Philippines and Vietnam resist China; Cambodia and Laos lean to Beijing. A Code of Conduct with China has been negotiated for years without conclusion. The 2016 arbitral award for the Philippines was rejected by China.
  • Non-interference limits action on human rights.
  • Weak secretariat and slow integration compared with the EU.
  • Great-power pressure from US-China rivalry and US tariffs in 2025-26.

Yet ASEAN has kept peace among members for nearly 60 years and shaped the region's architecture. Realists see it as a "talk shop"; constructivists see a nascent security community.

The Asia-Pacific Economic Cooperation forum was launched in Canberra in 1989, proposed by Australian Prime Minister Bob Hawke. It has 21 member economies, including the US, China, Japan, Russia, Australia, ASEAN states, Taiwan ("Chinese Taipei") and Hong Kong. It uses the word "economies" so that Taiwan and Hong Kong can join.

  • Open regionalism: lower barriers voluntarily, without discriminating against outsiders.
  • Non-binding decisions by consensus; leaders' meetings since 1993 (Blake Island, Seattle).
  • Bogor Goals (1994): free and open trade by 2010 for developed and 2020 for developing members.
  • Putrajaya Vision 2040 (2020) replaced them.

Korea hosted APEC in 2025 (Gyeongju) and China in 2026 (Shenzhen). Critics call APEC a summit photo-op; supporters say it builds norms and ideas that become trade deals (such as the CPTPP).

India applied to join APEC in 1991. In 1997 APEC froze new membership for ten years; the moratorium lapsed in 2007, but India was not admitted.

Why India is outside

  • Geography: India is not on the Pacific rim, though Russia and Peru joined in 1998.
  • Some members saw India's trade regime as too closed.
  • APEC's consensus rule lets any member block new entrants.
  • Fear that a large member would slow the group.

The US has at times said it "welcomes India's interest". India's Act East policy, the Indo-Pacific concept and its FTAs (ASEAN 2009, Japan and Korea 2010-11, Australia 2022) partly compensate. Membership would help India join regional supply chains.

The South Asian Association for Regional Cooperation was set up in Dhaka on 8 December 1985 by Bangladesh, Bhutan, India, the Maldives, Nepal, Pakistan and Sri Lanka. Afghanistan joined in 2007. The secretariat is in Kathmandu (1987). The idea came from Bangladesh's President Ziaur Rahman.

  • The Charter bars bilateral and contentious issues and needs unanimity.
  • Trade: SAPTA (1993, in force 1995) and SAFTA (2004, in force 2006).
  • Others: SAARC Development Fund, South Asian University (New Delhi, 2010), the SAARC Disaster Management Centre, and the SAARC satellite India launched in 2017 (as the South Asia Satellite, without Pakistan).

The last summit was the 18th, in Kathmandu in November 2014. The 19th, due in Islamabad in 2016, was called off after the Uri attack when India and others pulled out.

• India-Pakistan hostility and cross-border terrorism.
  • India's size: India accounts for most of the region's GDP and area, which raises fears of domination among neighbours.
  • Low intra-regional trade: only about 5% of South Asia's trade, among the lowest of any region.
  • Pakistan's blocking of connectivity, such as the SAARC motor vehicles agreement (2014).
  • No conflict-resolution role under the Charter.
  • China's rise: China is an observer and a major partner of most members.

In June 2025 China, Pakistan and Bangladesh held a trilateral meeting in Kunming. Reports spoke of a possible new grouping without India; Bangladesh denied it was an alliance. No formal bloc has been launched as of this writing.

Compare with ASEAN: a shared external threat, no single dominant member, and the habit of setting aside disputes.

cards.h: India's turn to BIMSTEC and Act East
cards.b:
• BIMSTEC (1997, Bangkok Declaration): Bangladesh, Bhutan, India, Myanmar, Nepal, Sri Lanka and Thailand. It links South and South-East Asia, and excludes Pakistan. Its Charter was adopted at the Colombo summit (2022). The 6th summit was in Bangkok (April 2025).
  • BBIN (2015) for road and power links.
  • Neighbourhood First policy and lines of credit; power trade with Nepal, Bhutan and Bangladesh.
  • ASEAN. Look East (1991-92) became Act East (2014). India became a sectoral partner (1992), dialogue partner (1995), summit partner (2002), strategic partner (2012) and comprehensive strategic partner (2022). The ASEAN-India goods agreement (2009) is under review because of India's trade deficit.
  • Connectivity: the India-Myanmar-Thailand Trilateral Highway and the Kaladan project.

"Why has ASEAN succeeded where SAARC has failed?"
"Explain the 'ASEAN Way'. Is it an asset or a liability?"
"Is BIMSTEC a viable alternative to SAARC?"
"Examine APEC's open regionalism. Should India seek membership?"

Structure: ASEAN origins, members, ASEAN Way, institutions, RCEP, limits (Myanmar, South China Sea). APEC: origin, open regionalism, Bogor, India's exclusion. SAARC: aims, achievements, the 2014-16 freeze and reasons. Comparison table. India: Act East, BIMSTEC, Kunming trilateral concern.

quiz.q: ASEAN was founded by the Bangkok Declaration of:
Which country became ASEAN's 11th member in October 2025?
quiz.w: At the 47th summit in Kuala Lumpur.

quiz.q: The ASEAN Charter entered into force in:
India withdrew from RCEP negotiations in:

quiz.w: On the initiative of Bob Hawke.

quiz.q: The last SAARC summit held was in:
BIMSTEC's Charter was adopted at the summit in:
quiz.w: The 5th summit, held virtually from Colombo.
